learningObjective: Reason about how a runtime decides where to place each op and tensor when the graph mixes CPU-only ops, GPU-native ops, and host↔device transfers.

canonicalClaims.claim: Device placement passes insert explicit host↔device transfer ops at boundaries between differently placed ops, and placement heuristics minimize the number of transitions on the critical path because transfer cost can dominate fine-grained kernels.
conditions: The runtime supports mixed CPU/GPU execution.
Host and device have distinct memory spaces connected by PCIe or NVLink.
nonImplications: Does not imply that all CPU ops should move to GPU; a round-trip may be more expensive than running the op on the slower device.
Does not imply transfer cost is zero on NVLink; NVLink is faster than PCIe but still non-zero.

misconceptions.claim: Device tags are advisory; the runtime can promote a CPU kernel to run on GPU.
misconceptions.whyWrong: An op with only a CPU implementation lacks a GPU kernel; there is no auto-promotion.

misconceptions.claim: Host↔device transfers are cheap and can be ignored in placement.
misconceptions.whyWrong: PCIe transfers cost microseconds to milliseconds and often dominate small ops; NVLink is faster but non-zero.

misconceptions.claim: Placing every op on the GPU is always optimal.
misconceptions.whyWrong: For small CPU-friendly ops the round-trip cost can exceed the GPU speedup.

misconceptions.claim: Transfer ops are inserted at run time based on tensor addresses.
misconceptions.whyWrong: Transfer ops are inserted at compile-time by a placement pass and recorded in the plan.
